content.body:
title = Basic Chat Communication 1.0.label = Basic Layout
# Clear or detune Radio 3 to be blank.
1.1.alert.modal = The chat window is the basic way to communicate with other players in Battleground Europe.[NL][NL]It has 6 "radios" you can transmit and receive messsages on. Each radio can be tuned to one of a number of available channels.
1.1.alert.hilite = chatview,target
1.1.alert1.modal = Each numbered radio (1-6) can be accessed via the same numbered function keys (F1-F6).[NL][NL]The label of the radio shows the channel that radio is tuned to.
1.1.alert1.hilite = channels,target
1.1.alert5 = Basic operation is simple: press Enter to open the text entry buffer, type a message, such as "Hello," and press Enter again to send the message.[NL][NL]Send "hello" to players in the area.
1.1.label = Chat Entry.
1.1.complete.hilite = chatinput
1.1.complete = Good. Other players on the channel, or close to you in the game world would have received the message.
1.2.alert.modal = When in the game world, the default chat channel (when you press Enter to chat, rather than one of the radios), is Area chat.[NL][NL]Friendly players within 100 meters will receive your message. This is an excellent way for players in the same area to coordinate.[NL][NL]Be careful though. Close enemy units see garbled text that might give your position away (although they will not receive your text message).
1.2.alert1 = Your Mission channel allows you to communicate with everyone on the same mission, regardless of their distance.[NL][NL]Select the Mission channel by pressing F1.
1.2.alert1.hilite = F1,target
1.2.label = Mission Channel
1.2.complete = Notice that the F1 channel header was highlighted and the chat bar opened.
1.3.alert = Enter some text and then press Enter to send on the Mission channel (radio F1).
1.3.label = Send Chat to Mission
1.3.complete = Good.
1.4.alert.modal = Your radios are automatically tuned to several channels but you may customize these.
1.4.alert1 = To tune a radio, click on the radio header you want to tune. Use {guicursor} to bring up the mouse if you are spawned in.[NL][NL]A List of available channels will be shown and you can click the channel you want that radio to be tuned to.[NL][NL]Click on the F3 radio header and select the Side channel.
1.4.alert1.hilite = F3,target
1.4.label = Tune the radio F3
1.4.complete = Good. Radio F3 is now tuned to the Side channel.
1.5.alert.modal = Chatting on radio F3 will now be sent to anyone on the "side" channel.[NL][NL]If you are allied, that includes French and British players. If you are axis, that will include all German players.
1.5.alert1.modal = A useful channel for new players is the Help channel, radio F6.[NL][NL]If you have any questions or need help, ask on this channel and other players or game managers will attempt to help you.
1.5.alert2.modal = The chat interface is also used to enter various commands such as adding someone to your friends list, accept a squad invitation, or send a private message.[NL][NL]These commands are entered by adding a dot (.) or slash (/) in front of the command.
1.5.alert3 = An example of such a command is the "time" command.[NL][NL]Open any radio, type "/time" and press Enter.
1.5.label = Entering Chat Commands
1.5.complete.modal = Good. You should see the time for your location and the server location the chat window.[NL][NL]A full list of available commands can be found in the Manuals tab under Chat Commands.
1.6.alert.modal = This concludes the basic chat tutorial.
1.6.label = End Tutorial
content.brief: Learn the basics of the chat system. Change channels, send private messages and chat with friends.
content.title: Basic Chat System
